questions.prompt: A 'hook' is —
questions.correctAnswer: an opening that grabs the listener's attention
hints: The start that pulls you in
questions.explanation: A hook is an opening that immediately grabs the listener's attention and makes them want more.

questions.prompt: A strong hook usually appears —
questions.correctAnswer: at the very beginning of the story
questions.explanation: The hook comes at the very start — the first thing that makes listeners lean in.

questions.prompt: Which is the STRONGEST hook?
questions.correctAnswer: "The night the lights went out, everything changed."
questions.explanation: An intriguing, specific opening like 'the night the lights went out' pulls listeners in far better than a flat start.

questions.prompt: A hook works by making the listener —
questions.correctAnswer: curious about what happens next
questions.explanation: A good hook sparks curiosity, making the listener want to find out what happens next.

questions.prompt: Starting a story with an interesting QUESTION can —
questions.correctAnswer: hook the audience
questions.explanation: Opening with an intriguing question is one way to hook an audience.

questions.prompt: Starting with ACTION (something happening) can —
questions.correctAnswer: grab attention right away
questions.explanation: Beginning with action drops listeners into something happening, grabbing attention immediately.

questions.prompt: A weak opening like 'This is a story about a dog' tends to —
questions.correctAnswer: not grab attention
questions.explanation: A flat, generic opening gives listeners nothing to grab onto and fails as a hook.

questions.prompt: A hook should connect to —
questions.correctAnswer: the rest of the story
questions.explanation: A hook should genuinely connect to the story, not be a random gimmick unrelated to what follows.

questions.prompt: Surprise or mystery in an opening can —
questions.correctAnswer: make listeners want to keep listening
questions.explanation: A touch of surprise or mystery in the opening makes listeners want to keep listening.

questions.prompt: Specific details in a hook are —
questions.correctAnswer: stronger than vague ones
questions.explanation: Specific, concrete details make a hook more vivid and gripping than vague generalities.

questions.prompt: A good hook can be —
questions.correctAnswer: an image, a question, action, or a surprising statement
questions.explanation: Hooks come in many forms: a striking image, an intriguing question, action, or a surprising statement.

questions.prompt: The purpose of a hook is to earn the listener's —
questions.correctAnswer: attention for the rest of the story
questions.explanation: A hook earns the listener's attention so they'll stay for the rest of the story.

questions.prompt: If a story starts slow, the fix is often to —
questions.correctAnswer: open with something more gripping
questions.explanation: A slow start is often fixed by opening with a more gripping moment or image.

questions.prompt: A hook that gives away the WHOLE story at once is —
questions.correctAnswer: usually too much (leaves nothing to discover)
questions.explanation: A hook should intrigue, not spoil — revealing everything at once leaves nothing to discover.

questions.prompt: Practicing your opening line helps because —
questions.correctAnswer: the first moments set the tone
questions.explanation: The first moments set the tone, so practicing your opening line is worth the effort.

questions.prompt: A hook can create an emotional pull by —
questions.correctAnswer: hinting at something at stake
questions.explanation: Hinting at something at stake creates an emotional pull that hooks the listener.

questions.prompt: Which hook best fits a scary story?
questions.correctAnswer: "No one had opened that door in a hundred years — until tonight."
questions.explanation: An ominous, specific opening matches a scary story and hooks the listener with dread and curiosity.

questions.prompt: A hook and the story's mood should —
questions.correctAnswer: match each other
questions.explanation: A hook should match the story's mood, setting the right tone from the first words.

questions.prompt: The best test of a hook is whether it makes the listener —
questions.correctAnswer: want to hear what happens next
questions.explanation: The best test of a hook: does it make the listener want to hear what happens next?

questions.prompt: A hook should be —
questions.correctAnswer: short and punchy, not long and slow
questions.explanation: A hook works best when it's short and punchy — grabbing attention quickly.

questions.prompt: Repeating an intriguing PHRASE at the start can —
questions.correctAnswer: create a memorable hook
questions.explanation: A memorable repeated phrase at the start can serve as a catchy, effective hook.

questions.prompt: A hook earns its place when it —
questions.correctAnswer: makes the audience commit to listening
questions.explanation: A hook earns its place by making the audience commit to listening to the rest.

questions.prompt: The BEST summary of the hook is —
questions.correctAnswer: a gripping opening that grabs attention and makes listeners want more
questions.explanation: The hook is a gripping opening that grabs attention and makes listeners want to hear the rest.

questions.prompt: Opening with a vivid IMAGE can hook listeners by —
questions.correctAnswer: painting a picture they want to explore
questions.explanation: A vivid opening image paints a picture listeners want to explore, hooking them into the story.

questions.prompt: A hook makes a promise to the listener that the story will —
questions.correctAnswer: be worth their attention
questions.explanation: A hook makes an implicit promise that the story will be worth the listener's attention.
